help.intro: The closing conversation of this module, in your own AI assistant with voice on: describing a place you know and planning something — where things are, where they go, and why you want to do what you plan. Copy the exercise in, say 'Los geht's', answer in full sentences; the score and corrections arrive at the end. With this conversation all the grammar of the course so far has been spoken aloud. The tutor listens for wo? + dative and wohin? + accusative, for weil and dass with the verb at the end, and for the natural order of details in the middle of a sentence — time before place: Ich fahre morgen nach Berlin, not the English way round.
help.tips[0].title: Time before place
help.tips[0].text: Ich fahre am Samstag mit dem Zug nach München — when, how, where. English says 'to Munich on Saturday'; German says the time first. (The full TeKaMoLo order comes later in the course.)
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: We're meeting at three outside the museum.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: I'm going to Munich by train on Saturday.
help.tips[0].trap: 'Ich fahre nach Berlin morgen' is understood but marked. Time first.
help.tips[0].check.q: Which word order sounds natural in German?
help.tips[0].check.why: German puts the time before the place: im Juli, then nach Spanien. The verb stays in second place.
help.tips[1].title: Give the reason with weil — and finish the clause
help.tips[1].text: Ich möchte ins Museum gehen, weil ich Kunst mag. Say the verb at the end and stop; don't add words after it.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: I suggest the café because it's opposite the cinema.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: I'd like to go to the park on Sunday because the weather is nice.
help.tips[1].check.why: In the weil-clause the verb gibt is the last word — finish the clause with it and stop.
help.tips[2].title: Propose, ask back, agree
help.tips[2].text: Wir könnten … · Was meinst du? · Gute Idee! / Lieber nicht, weil … — the three moves of planning together, with a friend, a colleague or a flatmate.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: We could go to the cinema on Saturday. What do you think?
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: Better not, because I have to work on Saturday. We could go on Sunday.
help.tips[2].check.q: Your friend says: „Wir könnten heute grillen. Was meinst du?“ You want to agree. What do you say?
help.tips[2].check.why: Gute Idee! is the agreeing move; Lieber nicht, weil … turns the plan down, and Was meinst du? just asks back.
help.remember[0]: Where things are: dative. Where they go: accusative. Why: weil, verb last.
help.remember[1]: Time before place, and ask back.
help.exam: Planning something together with a partner is a typical speaking task in the A2 exam — and how every weekend with friends gets organised.
help.hook: Plan a weekend out loud: propose an idea, give your reason with weil, and put the time before the place.

speaking.material:
Scene: I have just moved into the room in the picture and you are my friend Lena, who has come to help me set it up and then plan the weekend. We say du.
Do the picture description in character: Lena asks me to describe the room first.
Your role: ask where things are now and where they should go (Wo steht das Bett? Wohin stellen wir den Schreibtisch?), make one or two suggestions of your own and once ask what I think of one (so I answer with Ich finde, dass …), then ask what I want to do at the weekend and why.
My role: describe the room, say where each thing is and where it goes, and tell you what I plan and why I want to do it.
